'''Urmila Mahadev''' is an American mathematician and theoretical computer scientist known for her work in [[quantum computing]] and [[quantum cryptography]].

==Education and career==
Mahadev is originally from Los Angeles, California, where her parents are physicians. She became interested in quantum computing through a course with [[Leonard Adleman]] at the [[University of Southern California]],{{r|quanta}} where she graduated in 2010.{{r|grfp}}

She went to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] for graduate study, supported by a [[NSF-GRFP|National Science Foundation Graduate Research Fellowship]].{{r|grfp}}
As a student of [[Umesh Vazirani]] at Berkeley, Mahadev discovered [[interactive proof system]]s that could demonstrate with high certainty, to an observer using only classical computation, that a quantum computer has correctly performed a desired quantum-computing task.{{r|quanta}}

She completed her Ph.D. in 2018,{{r|mg}} and after continued postdoctoral research at Berkeley,{{r|quanta}} she became an assistant professor of computing and mathematical sciences at the [[California Institute of Technology]].{{r|caltech}}

==Recognition==
For her work on [[quantum verification]], Mahadev won the [[Machtey Award]] at the [[Symposium on Foundations of Computer Science]] in 2018, and in 2021 one of the three inaugural [[Maryam Mirzakhani New Frontiers Prize]]s for early-career achievements by women mathematicians.{{r|machtey}}{{r|mmnf}}
